newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea bond yields end lower on government steps.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea bond yields end lower on government steps.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds ended lower on Monday as South Korean President Kim Young-sam ordered his economic ministers to take steps to stabilise the local foreign exchange market, traders said.
They said Kim also asked the ministers to advance the opening of the local capital market to foreign investment to help promote the inflow of funds.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.50 pct vs Saturday's 12.66 pct
* 3-mth CDs end at 13.45 pct vs 13.60 pct
* Overnight average call rates at 13.02 pct vs 13.32 pct
"The yields would consolidate around 12.30 percent," a Samsung Securities broker said.
Three-month CD yields and overnight call rates also fell on expectation of stabilising foreign exchange market and improved liquidity conditions.
